definitions.explanation: An alcoholic beverage made from fermented grapes. The traditional Japanese word for wine, though ワイン (from English 'wine') is now more commonly used in everyday conversation.

examples.japanese: ぶどう{酒|しゅ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{一杯|いっぱい}→一杯：01793_ippai⟧⟦{飲|の}む→飲む：00322_nomu⟧。
examples.english: To have a glass of wine.

examples.japanese: ⟦{赤|あか}い→赤い：00585_akai⟧ぶどう{酒|しゅ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{好|す}き→好き：02355_suki⟧だ。

⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{地方|ちほう}→地方：02369_chihou⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{昔|むかし}→昔：01515_mukashi⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧ぶどう{酒|しゅ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{産地|さんち}→産地：04031_sanchi⟧⟦として→として：06802_toshite⟧⟦{知|し}られている→知る：00458_shiru⟧。
examples.english: This region has long been known as a wine-producing area.

notes: Compound of ぶどう (grapes) + {酒|しゅ} (alcohol/liquor). Also written as {葡萄酒|ぶどうしゅ} with kanji. In modern Japanese, ⟦ワイン→ワイン：01067_wain⟧ is far more common in everyday conversation; ぶどう{酒|しゅ} appears more in literary, formal, or traditional contexts. The {酒|しゅ} suffix is used for other types of alcohol as well: ⟦{日本酒|にほんしゅ}→日本酒：12954_nihonshu⟧ (sake), ⟦{梅酒|うめしゅ}→梅酒：16869_umeshu⟧ (plum wine), ⟦{焼酎|しょうちゅう}→焼酎：19874_shouchuu⟧ (distilled spirit). Japan's main wine-producing region is {山梨県|やまなしけん} (Yamanashi Prefecture).
